title: Five server change files still say they are not live, though the live database has all of them
what: The first lines of the entry machine, Pay MettleUp, forgot-PIN and plan-limits server changes say not applied. The live database holds their functions (entry machine admin and door calls, the MettleUp payment calls, the phone-code check, the plan-feature check), and later changes marked live depend on them. The feature map read those first lines and lists entry machines, Pay MettleUp and forgot PIN as hidden.
expected: Each server change file says its true live state and the date it went live.
evidence: data:live catalog read 2026-11-24 holds gate_save_punches, gate_take_commands, owner_entry_machines, owner_add_entry_machine, apply_gym_payment, owner_pay_mettleup, hq_mettleup_payments, _phone_proof, _phone_sig_ok, gym_has_feature, gym_state
who: whoever maintains the server and the feature map
fix_line: Rewrite the first line of each of the five files to say applied live, with the date

title: The test database has a plan-reading change the live server never got, so its known failure on live is normal
what: The change that lets both apps read which plan a gym is on was never put on the live server, but it sits in the middle of the change list, so every cloud test run builds a database that has it. The live security check already fails on its two functions and that failure is written off as expected. Both apps call it and, on live, quietly treat the answer as missing, so every feature stays on. The test database and the live one differ, and a real security failure on live would hide behind the known one.
expected: Either the change goes live with the owner's yes, or it is taken out of the list (or marked so the tests skip it) so the test database matches live and the live security check passes clean.
evidence: data:live catalog read 2026-11-24 has no member_gym_pack or owner_gym_pack
how_often: every test run and every live security check
fix_line: Decide 0046: apply it live or retire it, so test and live databases match

title: When a phone pop-up cannot be queued, the only trace is a database warning nobody reads
what: When the gym sends a message or offer, or answers a plan request, report request or shop order, a step queues the phone pop-up. If that step fails for any reason it is swallowed and only a database warning is written. Nobody watches those warnings, so a broken queue would lose every pop-up with no alert and no count.
expected: A failed queue step still never blocks the gym's action, but it is counted somewhere HQ looks (a failure row or an alert).
fix_line: Write a failure row HQ can see when a pop-up cannot be queued
